title.title: Dimension reduction in $L_p$ with $n^{o(1)}$ coordinates
title.subtitle: Claim: any $n$ points of $L_p$, $1<p<\infty$, $p \ne 2$, fit in $\ell_p^d$ with $d = n^{o(1)}$ at any fixed distortion

plain: Squeeze many points into few coordinates without warping distances much, in geometries beyond the usual one

beats.text: Coordinates needed to embed $n$ points with fixed distortion; schematic, constants omitted
Johnson–Lindenstrauss gives $\log n$ for $p = 2$; for $p<2$ the best was linear in $n$
Claim: $n^{o(1)}$ for every $p \ne 2$; drawn here for $p = 3/2$, $\exp(\sqrt{\log n})$

steps: Find one well-chosen random law for one-dimensional projections
Sample coordinates from it independently (Maurey's method)
Far fewer than $n$ coordinates then keep the distortion fixed

achievement.note: Exact isometric embeddings still need about $n^2$ coordinates

verify.detail: In Lean: the paper's Theorem 1.1 in full, self-contained
verify.ourCheck: From the paper and its Lean docs; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: n points at fixed distortion. For p below two, the best was linear in n.
Pick a clever random law for projections, then sample coordinates independently.
Claimed: far fewer coordinates, a sub-polynomial number.

sources.quote: d_p(n,D) <= exp(C_{p,D} (log n)^{gamma(p)}), gamma(p)=2-p for p<2 and 1-2/p for p>2; hence d=n^{o(1)}
Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984) gave O_D(log n) for p=2
Schechtman reached O_{p,D}(n) coordinates for p<2
Ball (Europ. J. Combin. 1990) gave the exact binom(n,2) bound
Constants are not uniform as p->1, p->2 or D->1; existential, no algorithm.
ComparatorChallenges/SubpolynomialLp.lean states the paper's Theorem 1.1 in full
